scenarios.title: Employees without matching departments
scenarios.question: List every employee with their department.
scenarios.cause: INNER JOIN drops 2 employees with a NULL DepartmentID and 1 whose department no longer exists.

scenarios.title: One-to-many fan-out
scenarios.question: Total paid and items bought per customer.
scenarios.cause: Joining OrderItems and Payments to the same order multiplies rows; the inner join to Payments also drops a customer with an unpaid order.

scenarios.title: Duplicate records
scenarios.question: How many distinct customers do we have?
scenarios.cause: Two people were entered twice with different capitalisation and spacing in their email.

scenarios.title: NOT IN with a NULL
scenarios.question: Which customers have never placed an order?
scenarios.cause: Orders contains a NULL CustomerID, so NOT IN is never true and the query returns nothing.

scenarios.title: Date boundary filtering
scenarios.question: Orders placed in January 2026.
scenarios.cause: BETWEEN ... AND '2026-01-31' ends at midnight, missing an order placed on 31 January at 16:45.

scenarios.title: AND/OR precedence
scenarios.question: Shipped or delivered orders going to Sri Lanka.
scenarios.cause: AND binds tighter than OR, so shipped orders to every country are included.

scenarios.title: COUNT versus COUNT DISTINCT
scenarios.question: Number of orders and units bought per customer.
scenarios.cause: After joining OrderItems there is one row per order line, so COUNT counts lines.

scenarios.title: Incorrect join key
scenarios.question: The lines of order 103 with their product names.
scenarios.cause: ProductID is compared with OrderItemID: the names are wrong and one line disappears.

scenarios.title: Unexpected aggregation granularity
scenarios.question: What is the average order value?
scenarios.cause: AVG runs over order lines (610 / 12) instead of orders (610 / 8).

scenarios.title: Missing join predicate
scenarios.question: The customer for each order placed in January 2026.
scenarios.cause: A comma join without a join predicate pairs each of the 4 orders with all 8 customers.
